chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him). I said, 'May I be your ransom! I bought a piece of land next to my estate for two thousand dirhams. When I paid the money, I was informed that the land was a waqf (endowment).' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The purchase of the waqf is not valid, and do not include the yield in your wealth; hand it over to the one to whom it was dedicated.' I said, 'I do not know its owner.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Give its yield in charity.'

key_terms.الْغَلَّةَ: Yield/produce (the income or crops generated by the property)
key_terms.وَقْفٌ: Endowment (property dedicated for religious or charitable purposes)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying land that turns out to be a waqf (endowment)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on purchasing a *waqf* (endowment) in good faith, establishing that while the transaction is valid, the produce (*ghallah*) does not become the buyer's personal property. He provides a practical solution for cases where the original dedicator is unknown: the yield should be given in charity (*sadaqah*), reflecting the Shia principle of preserving the endowment's purpose even when the specific beneficiary is unidentified. This ruling underscores the importance of distinguishing between ownership of the asset and the rights to its fruits in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ja’far Al Razaz, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from his father Ali Bin Rashid who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I bought a land by the side of my place for two thousand Dirhams. So when I paid the money, I was informed that the land was dedicated (Waqf)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not allowed to buy the dedicated (property), and do not included the yield in your wealth. Hand it over to the one who dedicated it’. I said, ‘I do not know its lord (owner)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give its yield in charity’.
en.sarwar: 35. Muhammad ibn Ja‘far al-Raziy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from abu Ali ibn Rashid who has narrated the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I have bought a land near by my assets for two thousand dirham. When I made payment, I was informed that the land is an endowment.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Buying an endowment is not permissible. You must not include its income in your assets. Give it back to its beneficiaries.’ I then said, ‘I do not know the beneficiaries.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Give its income in charity.’”
